definition: Dick called himself a Gnostic. The Gnostic study is at /studies/gnosticism; this topic indexes every mention by subsection, so the Gnostic material is reachable from the religion study as well.
editorial_notes: Every mention is listed by subsection, with its lane, date and editorial status. Interpretive prose for this tradition is not yet written; see the subsections for the material.

subsections.label: Sophia, Wisdom and the Holy Wisdom
subsections.description: Sophia as the fallen or redeeming feminine principle, and Hagia Sophia as the Holy Wisdom in his theology.

subsections.label: The Demiurge and the blind creator
subsections.description: The creator-god as ignorant or blind subordinate: Yaldabaoth, Ialdabaoth, Samael, the demiurge.

subsections.label: Anamnesis and recollection
subsections.description: Recollection of a true state before the fall, which Dick takes from Plato and from Gnostic texts.

subsections.label: Gnostic texts
subsections.description: The Gospel of Thomas, the Hymn of the Pearl, the Pistis Sophia and the Nag Hammadi library, as Dick knew them.

subsections.label: Gnostic (general)
subsections.description: Dick’s own uses of the words Gnostic and Gnosticism, without a specific doctrine or text.
